newsitem.title: USA: National City cites higher fee income.
newsitem.headline: National City cites higher fee income.

text.p: National City Corp said increased fee income, control over expenses and good asset quality contributed to a 17 percent rise in net income in the third quarter of 1996 compared to a year ago.

Net income was $185.8 million in the three months ended in September, equal to a record $0.82 per share fully diluted. The consensus earnings estimate in the Institutonal Brokers Estimate System was $0.82 per share.
Fee income in the third quarter rose 10.8 percent to $292.7 million from $264.2 million a year ago.
Loans at September 30 were $35.6 billion, up six percent from $33.7 billion on September 30, 1995.
National City said prior-year data was restated to reflect the acquisition of Integra Financial Corp.
At September 30, 1996, nonperforming assets totaled $176 million compared with $205 million at September 30, 1995.

Nonperforming assets at September 30, 1996 represented only 0.49 percent of loans and foreclosed real estate, compared to 0.61 percent a year ago. The allowance for loan losses as a percentage of loans was 1.99 percent at September 30, 1996.
